reading.ours: two units of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — an instrument check, and it is printed first because nothing below it means anything until it passes. The true ratio is a little UNDER 2: both sides pay the driving loop once, so the exact expectation is (2u + L) / (u + L) with L the loop and u one unit, which at sixteen dependent steps per unit puts it around 1.9. A reading below 1.5 means this process could not resolve a deliberate doubling, and the runner voids the report rather than printing prices under it.

reading.ours: one unit of arithmetic per iteration
reading.floor: the same body again, over its own copy of the same state
reading.caveat: NOT A PRICE — the noise floor. The two sides are identical code over identical, separately-allocated state, so the true ratio is 1.00 exactly and every departure from it printed here was produced by this machine at this moment. The rule that follows is the one the whole table is read under: NO RATIO CLOSER TO 1.00 THAN THIS GAP IS A READING. It also bounds the per-row noise figure, which is the same idea measured again inside every pair — each pair times its floor twice, once before our side and once after, and prints how far the two disagreed.

reading.ours: updateEntityColumn(value) on 128 roots, then channel.flush(); an OIMSingleComputed per root over its value column slot and one effect over all of them
reading.floor: startBatch(); value(v) on 128 rows; endBatch(); an alien computed per row over its value signal and one alien effect over all of them
reading.caveat: ONE OPERATION IS ONE FRAME: one column written on every one of 128 roots, and one settle. Each root has two columns, value and note; a derived value per root reads value only (value × 2), and one effect reads all 128 derived values, which is a derived collection wholly on screen. THE WRITTEN COLUMN IS THE ONE THE DERIVED VALUES READ, so both arms re-derive every value and run the effect once. Ours sources each derived value on the held column slot of value (slotContentOwner.holdColumn), so a note write does not reach it; alien has one signal per field, the shape every signal adapter in this bench uses, and batches the frame with startBatch/endBatch, since ours delivers once per frame. Ours is @oimdb/core from source: an OIMSingleEntity root written through entityContentService.updateEntityColumn, OIMSingleComputed nodes for anything derived, one effect from OIMEffectService, and channel.flush() as the settle. The floor is alien-signals 3.2: signal, computed, effect, and startBatch/endBatch where the row says so. Every write stores a new number from a counter, so no write on either arm is stopped by a same-value check. Each arm runs in its own process.
